title: The Real Truth Behind the Buying "Boring" Businesses Clickbait

 The Real Truth Behind the Buying "Boring" Businesses Clickbait
Hi Sara,
If you've spent even five minutes on YouTube this year, keep reading. If you do not consume that gross social media content, please go back to enjoying your classy life reading hardbound classic literature and playing your pristine vinyl collection of classic music. 
Now that it’s just us trashy YouTube consumers left, let’s speak freely.
You’ve probably seen the trend: videos promising the dream of buying a “boring business” like an HVAC company, car wash, or plumbing service that practically prints money while you lounge on a yacht.
I hate to burst the bubble, but as someone who’s been knee-deep in the mergers and acquisitions world for over a decade, I’m here to set the record straight.
Yes, these businesses can be profitable. No, they’re not as “hands-off” as YouTube makes them sound.
Here’s the truth:
They’re People-Intensive
These businesses thrive on their teams—but people also mean overhead and drama. Think payroll, health insurance, workman's comp, and endless management challenges. Scaling up? That just adds more moving parts. People have feelings and emergencies and generally require a lot of resources.

Customer Service Isn’t Optional
Whether it’s an HVAC technician or a car wash attendant, businesses that serve homeowners demand excellent customer service. And “excellent” doesn’t happen without constant oversight. Equipment breaks. Complaints roll in. Someone has to manage it all. A few negative reviews can quite literally bankrupt you.

You’ll Need More Than a Dream
Many first-time buyers think they’ll ramp up marketing and “manage from afar.” But unless you’re a professional management company with an executive team in place, this approach can be a recipe for disaster. Good luck finding a great operator- no one wants to take a meager salary and run a business soup to nuts for some guy living in Manhattan. 

Employees Fear Change
After an acquisition, employees often worry about layoffs or pay cuts. Stabilizing operations and winning their trust takes time—and money. And time is money…so you get the point.

Was that discouraging? I’m sorry! It can also be really great. If you’re ready to roll up your sleeves and tackle the operational side of business ownership, these industries can be lucrative and rewarding. But walking in with rose-colored glasses and think you pull something off based on what you learned from a 90-second TikTok? That’s a no-go.
The Best Kept Secret in the Business World
A lot of people I talk to are looking to buy a business. A great portion of those folks tell me they are ‘industry agnostic.’ They are very open-minded, but it’s also kind of an enormous thing to not narrow down. It’s like saying you’re ‘degree agnostic’ in college or ‘career agnostic’ after. Eventually, you have to decide or life will decide for you, right? 
A ton of acquisition happens in-home services (the general term for stuff like HVAC, plumbers, and electricians), and as an asset class, those are a pretty mixed bag. However, one industry consistently flies under the radar: accounting practices. They’re reasonably priced, have excellent margins (usually), and are often less resource-intensive than other businesses.
How many of us have looked for a new accountant only to be told that their accountant isn’t taking new clients? In what other industry is that even a thing?
